[Back to the lesson](cross-entropy.qmd) · [Learning path plan](review-path.qmd#scoring)

## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- For target q and prediction p, cross-entropy H(q,p) is the average of −log p(x) weighted by q(x).
- It equals H(q) + D_KL(q ∥ p). With q fixed, it is minimized when p matches q.
- If the target is concentrated on observed token y, it becomes −log p(y). Predictive entropy H(p) addresses uncertainty before observing the outcome.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

The model predicts p = (0.75, 0.25). Compare the cross-entropy in nats for q = (0.5, 0.5) and for the one-hot target q = (1, 0).

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

For the distributed target, the result is −0.5 ln(0.75) − 0.5 ln(0.25) ≈ 0.837 nats. With the one-hot target only the first term contributes, so the penalty is −ln(0.75) ≈ 0.288 nats.

</details>

To apply this penalty to a batch, see [the loss review sheet](revision-loss.qmd).
